subject: Pilot throughput vs. quality: recommended stack + prompt pack (HealthSync)
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@healthsync.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: performance questions and next steps

Hey Marcus / Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Couple of follow-ups from our side as we scope the pilot:

- Throughput: target ~150 TPS sustained for our peak routing window (1 hour).
- Latency: we'd like p95 < 300ms end-to-end if possible.
- Quality: hallucination on support transcripts is our top concern; we need precision on factual answers and stable behaviour when prompts change.

Can you share:
1) A short list of recommended models/configurations for an RAG pipeline (document retrieval + generator) that balances cost and quality?
2) Any Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS / latency percentiles) for those configs?
3) Example prompt sets / a prompt pack we can run against our sample queries?

I'm attaching a small set of sample queries and a snippet of transcripts (healthsync-sample-queries.csv) to help you pick the right baseline.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@healthsync.ai) for timing/POQ questions.

Appreciate a short recap and proposed next steps — ideally a 30–60m technical alignment next week.

Thanks,
Ari
Ari Kaplan
Head of AI Product, HealthSync
ari@healthsync.ai

Attachment: healthsync-sample-queries.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: performance questions and next steps

Hi Ari — great questions and thanks for the sample file. Below is a concise plan and recommended starting stack for the pilot. I tried to balance the throughput requirement and your quality constraints.

Summary recommendation (starter config):
- Retrieval: vector search on coarse, BM25 + FAISS hybrid for recall.
- Generator: Redwood-7B-ptq (8-bit) for initial pilot — best tradeoff for cost/quality at 150 TPS with batching.
- Fallback path: Redwood-1.3B-quant as low-cost, lower-latency option for non-critical routes.

Redwood-verified performance (baseline per-node):
- Redwood-7B-ptq @ 25-token avg prompt: sustained ~180 TPS with continuous batching, p50 ~45ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~430ms.
- Redwood-1.3B-quant @ 25-token avg prompt: sustained ~420 TPS, p50 ~18ms, p95 ~75ms.

Notes on quality/regression:
- We'll onboard your sample queries to our standard eval harness and compute precision/recall + factuality score.
- We recommend a small labelled prompt set for regression detection (we can seed with 200 examples).
- Default alerting threshold: regression alert at >1.5% absolute drop on the primary quality metric (you can tune).

Artifacts shared (links & attachments):
- Prompt pack (attached): redwood-prompt-pack-v1.zip — includes template prompts, few-shot examples, and a small eval harness.
- Pilot performance page: https://redwood.ai/perf/healthsync-pilot — live perf profiles and historical runs.
- Drive with sample evals: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/healthsync/prompt-pack
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HS-2027-04

Proposed next steps:
1) We run a 48-hour smoke run with your sample queries using Redwood-7B-ptq in us-west (we can mirror to eu if you need a geo copy).
2) We'll collect latency / token cost / quality metrics and share a short debrief.
3) Align on pilot SLA (p95 target + throughput) and sign a short pilot contract.

Would you be available for a 45-minute alignment tomorrow or Wed? I can also route this to our solutions engineer if you want a deep dive on quantization and batching.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-prompt-pack-v1.zip (ZIP, 1.2MB)

--

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: performance questions and next steps

Ari — adding a quick ops note from our side.

We can iterate the quantization profile to squeeze latency while keeping quality:
- Start: Redwood-7B-ptq (default PTQ profile) — good middle ground.
- If p95 is trending high, we'll apply an aggressive kv-cache-friendly kernel and a per-layer 4-bit split on attention matrices for the pilot window.

Question for you: do you expect many long-context queries (>=1024 tokens) during the peak? If so we'll need to tweak batch sizing; if not, the above will be fine.

I'll produce a short PDF with recommended quant profiles and expected delta in latency/costs and drop it into the drive.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: quant-profiles-summary.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

--

Thanks Marcus / Jordan — this is very helpful. A few quick answers and confirmations: 

- We can hit your suggested 150 TPS target for the smoke run; long-context queries are rare for now (avg ~120 token prompts).
- p95 target: yes, we'd like < 300ms; if you can hit ~200ms we'd be ecstatic.
- Please seed the eval harness with 200 labeled examples from our sample set and run the pilot against Redwood-7B-ptq as suggested.
- Procurement: we'll follow up on the pilot agreement but expect to approve a short-term PO by the end of next week.

When are you available for the 45-minute alignment? Tue 4/13 or Wed 4/14 morning (PST) both work for our team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the results.

Best,
Ari
Ari Kaplan
Head of AI Product, HealthSync
ari@healthsync.ai
